basis: Summarised from widely published general public-health advice (for example WHO and Government of India health guidance). NOT reviewed by a clinician. Must be checked and approved by a qualified medical professional, and translations by a native speaker, against current official sources before any real-world use.
disclaimer: This information is for general education only. It is not a diagnosis and does not replace a consultation with a doctor or health worker. Do not start or stop any medicine without medical advice. If you feel very unwell or are worried, visit a health centre.

emergency.title: Emergency: act immediately
emergency.intro: Do not wait or try home remedies if a person has any of these signs.
signs: Severe difficulty breathing, or lips and face turning blue
Chest pain or pressure that does not go away, especially with sweating or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
A fit (seizure) that does not stop, or the first fit a person has ever had
Sudden weakness or numbness on one side, a drooping face, or trouble speaking
Heavy bleeding that does not stop
Severe injury, burns, or suspected poisoning
In pregnancy: heavy bleeding, severe pain, or fits
A baby or child who is very drowsy, cannot drink, or is hard to wake
actions: Call an emergency number now, or ask someone nearby to call.
Go to the nearest hospital. If possible, do not travel alone.
Stay with the person and keep them calm. Do not give food or drink to someone who is unconscious or having a fit.
Use the Nearby Hospitals page to find the closest hospital with emergency care.

numbers.label: Ambulance (available in many states, including Karnataka)

symptoms.name: Fever
symptoms.about: Fever means the body temperature is higher than normal. It is a sign that the body is reacting to something, often an infection. It has many possible causes, so this page cannot tell you what is causing it.
selfCare: Rest and drink plenty of safe fluids.
Wear light clothes and keep the room comfortable.
Check the temperature again after a few hours and note how many days the fever lasts.
seeDoctorIf: Fever lasts more than 2 to 3 days.
The person is a baby under 3 months, an older adult, pregnant, or has a long-term illness.
There is a rash, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, or bleeding from the gums or nose.
Fever comes with repeated vomiting, or the person cannot drink fluids.
emergencyIf: Fits (seizures), confusion, or a stiff neck.
Very sleepy and hard to wake, or difficulty breathing.

symptoms.name: Cough or sore throat
symptoms.about: Cough and sore throat are common and usually come from short infections that get better on their own. Smoke, dust and allergies can also cause them.
selfCare: Drink warm fluids and rest.
Avoid smoke, including cooking smoke and tobacco, where possible.
Cover your mouth when coughing and wash your hands often to protect others.
seeDoctorIf: Cough lasts more than 2 weeks. This needs testing, for example for tuberculosis, especially with weight loss, night sweats or blood in the cough.
High fever lasts more than 3 days.
Wheezing, or throat pain that makes swallowing very difficult.
A young child, older adult or pregnant woman whose cough is getting worse.
emergencyIf: Struggling to breathe, or lips turning blue.

symptoms.name: Headache
symptoms.about: Most headaches are not serious. They are often linked to tiredness, stress, lack of sleep, not drinking enough water, or eye strain.
selfCare: Rest in a quiet place and drink water.
Try to keep regular meals and sleep times.
Limit long screen time, and get your eyes checked if headaches are frequent.
seeDoctorIf: Headaches that keep coming back or keep getting worse.
Headache with fever and vomiting, or with blurred vision.
Headache after a blow to the head.
A new, very sudden and severe headache.
emergencyIf: Sudden worst-ever headache, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, fits, or fainting.

symptoms.name: Diarrhoea or vomiting
symptoms.about: Loose watery stools or vomiting often come from infection or unsafe food or water. The main danger is losing too much body water (dehydration), especially in children and older people.
selfCare: Take small, frequent sips of safe fluids. Oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the standard recommendation; ask a health worker how to prepare and use it.
Keep eating normally if you can. Breastfeed babies as usual.
Use boiled or treated water, and wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.
seeDoctorIf: Diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days, or vomiting lasts more than 1 day.
Blood in the stool, or a high fever.
Signs of dehydration: very dry mouth, passing little or no urine, sunken eyes, extreme thirst or weakness.
The person is a baby, an older adult, or pregnant.
emergencyIf: Very drowsy, fainting, or unable to drink.

symptoms.name: Stomach pain
symptoms.about: Stomach pain has many causes, from indigestion and gas to problems that need urgent care. This page cannot tell which one it is.
selfCare: Rest and take sips of water.
Avoid very spicy or oily food, alcohol and tobacco until you feel better.
Note where the pain is, when it started, and what makes it better or worse, to tell the doctor.
seeDoctorIf: Pain lasts more than a day or keeps coming back.
Pain with fever, repeated vomiting, or yellow eyes or skin.
Black or bloody stools, or unexplained weight loss.
Any stomach pain during pregnancy.
emergencyIf: Severe pain that does not ease, a hard swollen belly, or vomiting blood.
Severe pain in a pregnant woman, or pain with heavy bleeding.

symptoms.name: Skin rash
symptoms.about: Rashes can be caused by heat, allergies, infections or skin conditions. Many are harmless, but some need a doctor.
selfCare: Keep the area clean and dry, and try not to scratch.
Avoid any new soap, cream or food you suspect caused it.
Wear loose cotton clothes.
seeDoctorIf: The rash spreads quickly, blisters, or becomes painful.
Rash with fever, or a rash after starting a new medicine.
Signs of infection: pus, warmth, swelling or spreading redness.
A rash that does not improve in a few days.
emergencyIf: Rash with swelling of the face or lips, or trouble breathing.

symptoms.name: Difficulty breathing
symptoms.about: Difficulty breathing can be serious. If it is severe, sudden or getting worse, do not wait to see if it passes.
selfCare: Sit upright and try to stay calm.
Loosen tight clothing and get fresh air.
Ask someone to stay with you and help you reach care.
seeDoctorIf: New breathlessness during light activity.
Breathlessness with a cough or fever lasting more than a few days.
Swollen feet together with breathlessness.
emergencyIf: Severe breathlessness, being unable to speak full sentences, blue lips, or chest pain.
Breathlessness in a baby or young child.

symptoms.name: Chest pain
symptoms.about: Chest pain has many causes, and some are life-threatening. Treat new or severe chest pain as an emergency until a doctor says otherwise.
selfCare: Stop what you are doing and sit down.
Ask someone to stay with you.
Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
seeDoctorIf: Mild chest discomfort that comes with effort and goes away with rest.
Sharp pain that is worse with deep breaths or coughing.
Burning pain after meals that keeps coming back.
emergencyIf: Chest pain or pressure lasting more than a few minutes, or spreading to the arm, neck or jaw.
Chest pain with sweating, nausea, breathlessness or fainting.
